The defect was the D-054 / testkit claim that the loader/exec enumeration is 'exhaustive for the PINNED Node version (22.x)', which named the wrong runtime. On candidate 05915c32 the testkit has no 'exhaustive', 'PINNED Node' or per-version enumeration. A grep of architecture.testkit.ts and architecture.test.ts for exhaustive|PINNED Node|Node 22.x|for the pinned finds only architecture.test.ts:352, a historical comment that explains why F-DG1-128's R1/R2 rows exist, not an exhaustiveness claim. The header (41-43) now says both checks are allow-lists that 'do not depend on the Node version' and names Node 24 as production and Node 22.18+ as the floor. D-055 supersedes the D-053/D-054 framing. I re-proved the module-level default-deny in a disposable clone (01-lint-probes.log): node:vm, worker_threads, inspector, net, http, sqlite, test, process, module, child_process, v8, wasi, tls, async_hooks, path-trick specifiers such as node:fs/../vm and node:crypto/../vm, dynamic import(), type-only imports and `export * from` are all violations. Self-check DD20 (`node:some-future-builtin`) shows that an unknown future built-in is denied. The version-naming defect is therefore dissolved. Caveat, tracked separately in F-DG1-130 rather than reopening this finding: version-independence covers which built-in modules may be imported, not the members of the allowed modules (crypto/fs/util), and those members can still change between Node versions.
